lines.speaker: Μίνως
lines.text: Let Sostratus the bandit here be thrown into Pyriphlegethon. Let the temple-robber be torn apart by the Chimaera. As for the tyrant, Hermes, stretch him out next to Tityus and let the vultures have his liver too. And you good people, be off at once to the Elysian Fields. Take up residence in the Isles of the Blest—a just reward for a just life.

lines.speaker: Σώστρατος
lines.text: Listen, Minos, and see if I don't have a fair point.

lines.speaker: Μίνως
lines.text: [sighs] I have to listen to you again? Haven't you already been convicted, Sostratus? You're a villain, you murdered all those people...

lines.speaker: Σώστρατος
lines.text: Convicted, yes. But consider whether I am justly punished.

lines.speaker: Μίνως
lines.text: Of course you are. Assuming it's just to pay for your crimes.

lines.speaker: Σώστρατος
lines.text: Still, answer me this, Minos. I have a very short question for you.

lines.speaker: Μίνως
lines.text: Speak. Just keep it short. We have the rest of the docket to clear.

lines.speaker: Σώστρατος
lines.text: Everything I did in my life—did I do it of my own free will, or was it spun for me by Fate?

lines.speaker: Σώστρατος
lines.text: So all the good people, and those of us deemed wicked—we were all just acting as her servants when we did these things?

lines.speaker: Μίνως
lines.text: Yes. Servants to Clotho. She prescribes exactly what every person must do the moment they are born.

lines.speaker: Σώστρατος
lines.text: Right. So suppose someone is forced by another to commit a murder. They have no power to refuse the person compelling them. An executioner obeying a judge, say, or a bodyguard obeying a tyrant. Who do you blame for the murder?

lines.speaker: Μίνως
lines.text: The judge or the tyrant, obviously. You certainly don't blame the sword. The sword is merely a tool serving the anger of the prime mover.

lines.speaker: Σώστρατος
lines.text: Excellent, Minos. Thank you for expanding on my example. Now, what if someone is sent by his master to deliver a gift of gold or silver? Who gets the gratitude? Who gets recorded as the benefactor?

lines.speaker: Μίνως
lines.text: The master who sent it, Sostratus. The carrier is just a courier.

lines.speaker: Σώστρατος
lines.text: So do you see how unjust you're being? You're punishing us for being servants to Clotho's commands, and you're rewarding these people for delivering someone else's generosity. After all, no one could possibly argue that we have the power to resist absolute necessity.

lines.speaker: Μίνως
lines.text: [long pause] Sostratus, if you look closely enough, you'll find plenty of things down here that don't stand up to strict logic. But you shall have the benefit of your argument. It seems you are not just a bandit, but quite the philosopher. Hermes, let him go. Cancel his punishment. [pause] Just... make sure you don't teach the rest of the dead to ask the same questions.
